fact: At an 8 October 2026 meeting chaired by the posts and telecoms minister with the universal service fund (FDSU) and four operators, a solar microsite solution from Africa Mobile Networks was presented for rural and peri-urban coverage, with 50 pilot sites planned, and the authorities aim to connect 68 million rural people by 2035.
The universal service fund (FDSU) signed subsidy agreements in August 2026 with Vodacom, Airtel, Africell and Orange for at least 40 towers in peri-urban and rural areas, per a ministry communique.

The FDSU signed its first subsidy agreements with Airtel, Vodacom, Orange and Africell for a first phase of 40 sites under the Universal Connectivity Project in rural and peri-urban areas, with about 300 sites next and 3,000 settlements by 2030.

The FDSU published a status assessment on 7 August 2026 and is developing a national strategy to expand mobile and broadband connectivity in underserved rural and peri-urban communities, where about 4.3 million people in nearly 3,000 localities lack coverage.

The FDSU runs a National Strategy for Universal Connectivity 2026-2035 to extend telecoms access in rural and peri-urban areas, with a phase 0 of 40 pilot sites and a phase 1 of about 300 sites in five zones, selected by a scoring framework.

fact: The universal service fund FDSU launched construction of its first pilot telecom sites at Nkamba on 30 May 2026, the first time the state directly finances telecom infrastructure for rural and peri-urban populations, within a national connectivity programme to connect all 145 territories (ACTUALITE.CD).

The secretary general of Internet Society RDC says the universal service fund, created in 2020 to support connectivity in rural and peri-urban areas, is still not available (ACTUALITE.CD, 19 February 2025).
